title: The Door to the Pass
hook: Eastbound and rolling. The street is empty.
scene: Overcast midday daylight on a two-lane downtown street heading east, wet asphalt edge to edge. Flat gray light, no sun, no cast shadows. The Menace is rolling east in the eastbound travel lane on that wet asphalt — wheels turning, in-lane motion. The street is empty of other vehicles and empty of people. There is no marked crosswalk and no painted stop line in this stretch. Brick downtown sits behind the car to the west. Ahead, the same two-lane continues empty toward the east. Both cats are a sound in the closed carrier on the floor. The mountain pass is still closed to her.
debrief: The Beetle is rolling east on an empty wet street. Downtown sits behind it. The eastbound continues empty ahead.

source.teaching_target: Establishing: Menace rolling east on an empty two-lane; city behind; no yield, no pedestrian, no crosswalk.

image_brief.camera_pose: Shallower high-oblique aerial, about forty degrees off vertical, looking along travel so the rear of the faded pink Beetle is nearer the camera and the body recedes east away toward the top of the frame. Off-nadir, not map-flat plan-view, not eye-level, not a steep three-quarter, not a front portrait. Photoreal overcast midday: flat gray-white sky, no sun disk, no cast shadows. Continuous empty wet two-lane — no marked crosswalk, no white bars, no stop line, no pedestrian, no other vehicles. Brick downtown sits behind the car to the west, nearer the camera. Empty eastbound continues ahead. The Beetle is a small mass rolling in-lane, wheels turning. Soft implied plow on the bull-bar nose is enough; do not force a full-width blade. NOT a yield scene. NOT a stopped hold. NOT a pedestrian-in-the-paint shot.
